b: HubSpot AI notetaker helps sales teams capture, transcribe, and analyze customer meetings. It then turns those conversations into summaries and suggested next steps for reps, as well as coaching and pipeline insights for managers.
Notetaker helps reps save time and focus on the customer during sales calls, rather than frantically scribbling notes, reconstructing the conversation afterward, or missing important details.

Here’s how HubSpot AI notetaker works: A Super Admin enables it, reps connect their calendars, and notetaker joins eligible Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams meetings. After each meeting, reps can review and approve the summaries, tasks, and CRM updates it suggests. Managers can build in and adjust controls throughout the process, whether you’re a VP of Sales planning a team-wide rollout or a RevOps admin responsible for setup and governance.

This guide explains what notetaker is, who can use it, how the bot joins meetings and handles consent, how reps review its recommendations, how managers can use meeting summaries for coaching, and more.

What is HubSpot AI notetaker, and who can use it?

HubSpot AI notetaker captures, transcribes, summarizes, and logs eligible sales meetings in HubSpot. When a meeting ends, notetaker analyzes the transcript and related deal information to generate a summary, suggest property updates for deals, calls, and meetings, surface action items you can turn into tasks, and draft a follow-up email.

Notetaker is part of HubSpot’s Sales Hub and integrates with the Smart CRM. As a result, notetaker stores all recordings in the CRM contact record. This centralization avoids data silos, but reps still control what’s stored in contact records because notetaker lets them approve, edit, or dismiss suggestions.

Notetaker is available to users on Sales Hub and Service Hub Professional and Enterprise plans. Each user needs an assigned Sales or Service seat. It works with Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, and Zoom without requiring an additional app installation.
How to Make Meetings Eligible for Notetaker

For a meeting to qualify, it must be created or stored in HubSpot, include at least one CRM contact whose email domain differs from your account’s domain, and have its location set to Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, or Zoom. The contact rule matters because it lets notetaker sidestep internal meetings, such as a team standup, and focus on customer and prospect conversations.
How to Enable and Configure HubSpot AI Notetaker
It takes only a few minutes to set up notetaker in HubSpot once initial requirements are met. Note the following channel-specific prerequisites teams need to know before using notetaker:
Each user must connect their calendar.
For Zoom users, the meeting host must have local recording turned on. In other words, the standard call recording on Zoom should be set to save to the host’s computer.
For Google Meet users, the host must join the call to manually admit notetaker or pre-set their Google Meet access settings to “Open” to automatically admit participants.
Daily limit: Each HubSpot user can invite notetaker to as many as 40 meetings per day.
Recurring meetings: Notetaker joins recurring meetings only if you opt into the Sync Recurring Meetings to HubSpot beta.
Timing: HubSpot sends the join instruction 30 minutes before a meeting starts, so setting changes may not apply to meetings started inside that window.
Step-by-Step: How to Configure Notetaker in HubSpot
Step 1: Turn on the notetaker feature for the account.
Only Super Admins can enable the notetaker feature for a HubSpot account and adjust its default settings.
Click the settings icon in the top navigation bar, then click Notetaker in the left sidebar.
Under General settings, toggle on Conversation recording, Transcription and analysis, and Meetings.
Under Meetings, click HubSpot’s notetaker bot settings. The bot’s settings page opens in a new tab.
Choose how notetaker joins. The notetaker auto-join checkbox is selected by default. Clear it if you’d rather have users invite notetaker manually.

Choose who gets access. Select Automatically grant eligible users notetaker access to cover every Sales or Service seat. Or select Manually grant users with sales or service seats notetaker access, click Select users, check the boxes, and click Save selections.
Optionally, set a name. By default, the bot joins as your brand name’s notetaker. Select Custom notetaker name to change it.
Pick an announcement. Choose Verbal and chat announcement (and select a language and voice) or Chat message announcement only.
Use the Join before meeting start dropdown to set when the bot arrives.
Decide on consent. Toggle on Require explicit consent to request consent by email before each meeting. If any participant declines or doesn’t respond, the meeting isn’t recorded.
Step 2: Let reps adjust their own settings.

Users with an assigned Sales seat and notetaker access can modify their notetaker settings. For example, they can determine whether notetaker joins calls automatically or only when the rep invites it. To make this change, go to:
Settings > General > Calendar and find notetaker settings.
Clear notetaker auto-join, and click Save.
HubSpot can use a transcript to recommend CRM updates. Super Admins decide which properties are eligible for such recommendations.
Go to Settings > Data Management > Data Capture and select Use smart data capture.
Use the dropdown to choose an object type, then add properties with the Add [object] property menu.
For each property, check Automated to approve suggestions automatically, or clear it to require manual review. Call outcome and Meeting outcome are Automated by default.

Pro tip: Mind the credits, though. Each custom property in smart data capture settings consumes 10 credits per transcript run. Run five transcripts across five custom properties, and you’ve used 250 credits.
Standard properties don’t consume credits. One practical approach: Keep ‘Automated’ off for fields that feed your forecast, so a rep sees every change before it lands.
Step 4: Control notetaker meeting by meeting.

When scheduling: On a CRM record, click Schedule a meeting. Then, select Invite notetaker to meeting in the notetaker section. If you book on behalf of another host, the host’s default setting applies.
To check an existing meeting: Open the record, expand the meeting in the Activity timeline, and look for a green dot with the bot’s name. To change it, click Actions > Edit and toggle the checkbox.
As the host: Go to Sales > Calendar > Upcoming meetings, open the meeting, and toggle Invite notetaker on or off.
How HubSpot AI notetaker Joins Meetings and Handles Consent
When notetaker is invited to an eligible meeting, it joins and announces itself through an audio message, a chat message, and a pop-up. The behavior differs slightly by platform:

Google Meet and Microsoft Teams: notetaker receives recording permission as soon as it joins. After a few seconds, it plays an audio message and posts a chat message. It posts the chat once only, so people who join the call later will not see it unless the host pins the message.

Zoom: The host gets a pop-up asking to approve recording and must click Approve. Once approved, an audio message plays, and each participant who joins receives a chat message from notetaker explaining that it’s being recorded and that they should tell the host if they don’t want to be recorded.
Don’t want notetaker to join automatically? Set up a waiting room. Once the meeting host joins, they’ll receive a notification that the notetaker is waiting to join.
If the host denies access, notetaker doesn’t join.
If it waits more than five minutes without being admitted, it leaves.
Note: Allowing notetaker to join the meeting will automatically permit it to record. The audio and chat messages described above will appear.
How to Coach With HubSpot AI Notetaker Summaries

Sales managers use meeting summaries for coaching and pipeline inspection. After each meeting, HubSpot creates a call/meeting record tied to the relevant CRM records. The platform then adds the recording, transcript, meeting summary, action items, and CRM property suggestions to it. Managers can open one record and see what was said alongside the deal it belongs to. With this insight, they can establish a review cadence while protecting access, and connect insights to coaching and pipeline decisions.
A predictable review cadence matters more than checking every single call.
Find the right calls quickly. The Calls Index can be filtered by user, team, call outcome, and duration.
Pick a small, consistent sample. Aim to review one ot two calls per week with each rep. Focus more on lost deals to improve future win rate and track the post-coaching win rates.

Start with the summary, then go deeper. The AI-generated call summary sits at the bottom of the recording page for Sales Hub or Service Hub Professional and Enterprise users. Open the recording or transcript only when the summary points to a coachable moment, such as a missed discovery question or a weak response to an objection.
Coach inside the record. On Professional and Enterprise, you can add threaded inline comments to transcripts. This keeps feedback attached to the exact moment in the call.
Recordings contain customer conversations and colleague conversations, so set the guardrails before you start coaching.

Control who gets notetaker. Once notetaker is turned on at the account level, it can be configured per user. Managers can grant access automatically to all users with an assigned Sales Hub Professional or Enterprise seat, or manually to specific users.
Respect consent. Notetaker starts recording based on the meeting host’s permissions. If any invitee doesn’t consent, they will not join.

Inform participants that notetaker is recording. Because notetaker joins all scheduled meetings when turned on unless a user opts out, colleagues may be recorded too. It’s best practice to state upfront that the meeting is being recorded for coaching purposes (if applicable).
Know the retention period. Recordings are retained for two years in HubSpot’s file manager. Make sure this fits your internal data policy.
Connect insights to coaching and pipeline decisions.
Sales managers can use the same summary to review how the rep performed and what the deal looks like.
Coaching: Notetaker can help spot patterns in rep summaries, such as repeatedly skipped qualification questions or lack of clear next steps.
Pipeline inspection: Managers can compare the summary and action items against the deal stage and close date to verify the forecast.
CRM hygiene: Notetaker also produces CRM property suggestions to check whether deal fields reflect what the buyer said. Managers can approve,
Follow-through: Review next steps, set action items and follow-up notifications, and draft emails.
Turn insights into pipeline movement with Smart Deal Progression.

Meeting transcripts provide input to Smart Deal Progression for CRM suggestions, follow-up emails, and next tasks. While the summary shows a manager what happened in a meeting, Smart Deal Progression turns that conversation into updates that keep the deal record accurate.
Notetaker captures the conversation. The transcript can come from HubSpot’s own notetaker or from a connected meeting app such as Zoom, Teams, or Google Meet.
Deal context is added. Deal Progression runs the captured transcript against your full deal history and CRM context. This is why its suggestions are specific to the deal rather than generic.
The rep gets suggestions. It suggests changes to both default and custom properties, drafts contextual follow-up emails, and surfaces next steps. Custom property updates are powered by Data Agent.
A human approves. Reps review and refine the suggestions, then apply them with one click. Nothing should change on the deal until the rep confirms it.
Coach on follow-up quality. The drafted email and tasks are a starting point. As a manager, instruct and check that reps tailor their follow-ups and don’t send generic ones.
Frequently Asked Questions About HubSpot AI Notetaker
Does HubSpot AI notetaker work with Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams?
Yes. HubSpot AI notetaker works with the three major video conferencing platforms, including Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams.
Can reps choose not to record a specific meeting?

Yes. HubSpot lets Super Admins turn on meeting recordings for all team members with a Sales Hub seat. However, reps can change the meeting invitation setting. Also, any participant with permission to remove participants during a call can remove the notetaker bot directly from the video conferencing platform.
Where do AI summaries and action items appear in the CRM?

Meeting recordings, transcripts, and summaries are stored on the meeting record. HubSpot’s documented sales workspace review includes summaries and suggested follow-up activities; availability depends on account access.
How does consent work for recorded meetings?
Notetaker announces its presence via a chat message when it joins a meeting. This notification is sent to all participants in the meeting chat and cannot be turned off.

Notetaker also offers optional pre-meeting consent, letting admins turn on a setting that sends each meeting invitee a consent email in advance. Notetaker only joins the email if they all invite consent to being recorded.
Which plans include HubSpot AI notetaker?
HubSpot’s AI notetaker is available on the Starter, Professional, and Enterprise plans of HubSpot’s Sales and Service Hub.
Making the Most of Your Meetings

HubSpot AI notetaker lets sales teams spend less time taking notes and more time with customers. Reps stay in control by approving every suggested CRM update, task, and follow-up email. With more visibility, managers can coach on specific moments and check the forecast against what the buyer actually said.

Before rolling notetaker out, settle on guardrails: who gets access, how you’ll tell participants they’re being recorded, and which properties should be automated. With those in place, notetaker can become a dependable part of how teams run meetings.
